response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT e.ordersmark AS ordersmark, o.timespan AS timespan, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.timespan), with_tif AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, AVG(avg_fill) OVER (PARTITION BY timespan) AS tif_avg, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM per_order) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, avg_fill - tif_avg AS excess_over_tif_avg, rnk AS rank_in_timespan FROM with_tif WHERE avg_fill > tif_avg AND rnk <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, rnk, ordersmark

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique per order (as documented), so grouping executions by ordersmark gives one row per order with a single timespan.

Orders whose executions all have NULL fillcount have a NULL average. They are excluded from the time-in-force mean and from the strictly-above filter, but still take part in the ranking, at the end. Because every kept order is above the mean, ranks are the same whether computed before or after the filter.
